name: Bryant Park Fall Migration Birding Tours
why: Guided fall migration birding walks with urban naturalist Gabriel Willow; runs Tuesdays 8–9am and Thursdays/Fridays 5–6pm through October 10.

name: Rooftop Cinema Club
why: Outdoor rooftop movie screenings through September including Amélie, Casablanca, Get Out, Hocus Pocus, Sinners, and more; wireless headphones provided.

name: Teenage Malady Screening Series
why: Mini series exploring the darker, more unsettling side of adolescence through River's Edge, The Virgin Suicides, Elephant, and Totally F***ed Up; runs through September 24.

name: Woven Together: Touch Exhibition Opening
why: Opening reception for an annual fiber art exhibition featuring works by artists from the disability arts community designed to be experienced through touch; runs through 9/30.

name: Metropolitan Opera Summer HD Festival
why: Encore screenings from the Met's Live in HD series projected onto the opera house's façade at Lincoln Center Plaza; 2,500 seats first come, first served.

name: 9th Annual Rockaway Film Festival
why: Five days of indie films, shorts, live music, and filmmaker Q&As; highlights include a documentary with live music by TV on the Radio's Kyp Malone and a film by How to with John Wilson creator John Wilson.

name: Morningside Lights Lantern-Building Workshops
why: Help build the giant lanterns for the 15th annual Morningside Lights procession on September 19; workshops run 9/12–18 on the Miller Theatre stage, no experience needed.

name: SummerStage: Samara Joy + Christian McBride
why: Samara Joy and Christian McBride celebrate Verve Records' 70th anniversary, with Mei Semones + Friends playing the music of Getz/Gilberto and a Sparklmami DJ set.

name: Our Bar Theatre: 'Power'
why: Theater artists perform original scenes that could actually happen in the bar that night; tonight's theme is 'Power.' A Bud Light is included with admission.

name: 17th Annual NYC Unicycle Festival
why: Long-distance unicycle rides from Battery Park to Central Park and across the Brooklyn Bridge to Coney Island, followed by a weekend of games, demonstrations, and a learn-to-ride area in Jackson Heights.

name: ETHEL at the Cultural Center at St. John's
why: Grammy-winning string quartet ETHEL opens Greenpoint's newly christened cultural and performing arts center at St. John's Lutheran Church.

name: Bryant Park Picnic Performances: Grace Kelly + Ashni
why: Asian American Arts Alliance presents an evening of R&B, electropop, and smooth and nu jazz with Grace Kelly and Ashni; blankets and bistro chairs provided.

name: Loxfest
why: Annual bagel-and-lox festival returns to Pier 17 with local bagels, smoked fish, tastings, music, and more.

name: Enterprise Security in the Age of AI
why: Panel with senior security and AI leaders on what real protection looks like when attacks move at machine speed and frontier cyber capability sits inside a handful of labs.

name: Harness Engineering & Model Wrangling Hackathon
why: One-day NYC hackathon to build persistent, adaptive AI agents with MongoDB Atlas, Vector Search, and Agentic Memory; finalists showcase projects live at MongoDB.local NYC on September 30.

name: Grand Central Terminal Tour
source: Municipal Art Society of New York
via: Municipal Art Society of New York
why: MAS Docents lead guided tours of Grand Central Terminal exploring its history and architecture; tours are mostly indoors and run on multiple dates and times.

name: Western Bed-Stuy Tour
source: Municipal Art Society of New York
via: Municipal Art Society of New York
why: Guided architectural and neighborhood walking tour of Western Bedford-Stuyvesant with Suzanne Spellen; tours typically last 90 minutes to two hours.

name: Antonin Dvořák in New York Tour
source: Municipal Art Society of New York
via: Municipal Art Society of New York
why: Walking tour with Francis Morrone retracing Antonin Dvořák's footsteps in New York, exploring the sites connected to his years composing in the city.

name: dapperQ presents Legacy
why: 11th year of New York Fashion Week's largest LGBTQIA+ fashion show presented by dapperQ, with happy hour, shopping from queer designers, and a runway presentation of new designs from ATASHI RTW, BoiPKG, DYKEMINT, and others.

name: Art of Manga
why: First major exhibition in the Americas to explore manga as an art form, featuring 600+ original artworks from beloved series including Inuyasha, JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, ONE PIECE, and more. Opens October 3.

name: Fall Fête
why: After-hours season launch party with music, gallery access, food and drink, and performances by Otaku Choir, DJ Jon Ray, Acky Bright, and Shia Ho; cosplay encouraged. Hosted by Miss Ma'am She.

name: Art History Happy Hour: Sculpting the Senses
why: Short talks on designer Iris van Herpen from curator Matthew Yokobosky, mathematician Ingrid Daubechies, and art history professor Lynn Gamwell, followed by access to Van Herpen's haute couture works in Sculpting the Senses; one specialty drink included.

name: Moomin Fest at NYBG
why: Final-day celebration of the Summer of Moomin with nature walks, sketching sessions, a film screening and panel discussion with Maria Popova and Kate Zambreno, and Moomin-themed pop-ups on Daffodil Hill.

name: Growing America
why: Exhibition tracing 250 years of American history through the plants and foods that shaped it, with historical documents in the Mertz Library and a living display at the Barnsley Beds; through October 18.

name: Bird Tours with NYC Bird Alliance at NYBG
why: Expert bird guide from NYC Bird Alliance leads a birding tour of NYBG's diverse landscape; also September 19, October 3 and 18.

name: Climate Week NYC at NYBG
why: Talks with leading urban ecologists and conservationists on how to Nature Your City, plus a partner showcase and Farmers Market; NYBG offers free grounds admission on September 23 for all Climate Week events.

name: NYBG 5K Fun Run
why: Second annual 5K run through the Garden's most scenic areas to celebrate the end of Climate Week NYC; proceeds support biodiversity protection and plant-based climate solutions.

name: NYBG Farmers Market
why: Weekly market with fresh locally grown produce, baked goods, and artisanal items from rotating vendors; every Wednesday 10am–2pm.

name: America's Civic Gospel: Geraldine Brooks, Jill Lepore & Jane Kamensky
why: Geraldine Brooks, Jill Lepore, and Jane Kamensky in conversation with Ted Gioia on America's civic traditions and democratic ideals.

name: Lincoln in the Bardo: George Saunders, Missy Mazzoli & Royce Vavrek
why: George Saunders, composer Missy Mazzoli, and librettist Royce Vavrek discuss the opera adaptation of Lincoln in the Bardo at LIVE from NYPL.

name: Pathways to Publishing: Expo for Aspiring Authors
why: Free expo for writers hoping to get published, with hands-on workshops and panels with authors, editors, agents, and community writing organizations.

name: TechConnect: Learn About AI Workshop Series
why: Three-workshop series covering AI's technological foundations, how to evaluate its outputs, its risks, and specific practical tasks; at NYPL branches across the Bronx, Manhattan, and Staten Island.

name: Declaring America: 1776 and Beyond
why: Multi-gallery exhibition at the Schwarzman Building unpacking the complex, diverse stories of the American Revolution through founding documents, protest ephemera, artworks, and artifacts; through January 10, 2027.

name: To Uncover and Reveal to the World: Arturo Schomburg's Library
venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
why: Over 100 objects from the collection Arturo Schomburg assembled—books, manuscripts, and art documenting the African diaspora—many on display for the first time since the library acquired them in 1926; through December 5.

name: Martha Graham: The Mother of Psychological Dance
why: Large-scale exhibition drawing from the Jerome Robbins Dance Division's Martha Graham archive, featuring set pieces by Isamu Noguchi and costumes designed by Graham herself; through November 7.

name: Unleashed: Pets of the Performing Arts
why: Exhibition showcasing animals behind the artists—from Billie Holiday's boxer Mister to Anna Pavlova's pet swan Jack—drawn from the Library for the Performing Arts' archives; through February 6, 2027.

name: Walking Tour: Downtown New York Architecture in 1776
why: Guided walking tour exploring what downtown New York looked like in 1776—the streets, buildings, and urban landscape of the Revolutionary-era city.

name: Medium and Message: An Introduction to Exhibition Design
why: Talk introducing the principles and practice of exhibition design at the Center for Architecture.

name: Recipe for a Room 2026: Places for Repair
why: Annual architecture talk at the Center for Architecture exploring spaces designed for repair—both physical and social—in the built environment.

name: The Fling 2026 at Fort Greene Park
why: Annual outdoor dance party and fundraiser under string lights at Monument Plaza, with sets from Brooklyn father-son DJ duo Saint James Joy and the Brooklyn Music School Jazz Ensemble; catered dinner available.

name: Activity Center at the Play Lawns
why: Free lawn games, cornhole, binoculars, scavenger hunts, and more at the bright blue container by the Play Lawns; every weekend through November 1, 12–4pm.

name: Weekly Bird Tours on Governors Island
why: Guided weekend birding tours of Governors Island's unique 120-acre landscape.

name: Allen Ginsberg at 100
why: Thomas Bartlett leads five nights celebrating 100 years of Allen Ginsberg with a rotating roster including Laurie Anderson, Rufus Wainwright, Bill Frisell, Taylor Mac, and Marc Ribot performing kaleidoscopic musical interpretations of the poet's work.

name: Papi Juice Party
why: Brooklyn's beloved queer and QTPOC nightlife collective Papi Juice brings their all-night dance party to Little Island for the final Friday of six-week residency.

name: Free Friday Nights at the Whitney Museum
why: Final free Friday evening at the Whitney (through September 4), with access to all exhibitions, DJ sets, live music, and city-view drinks from 5–10pm.

name: 29th Annual Bus Festival
why: 29th annual vintage vehicle extravaganza celebrating the Transit Museum's 50th anniversary; climb aboard historic buses, take surface transit trivia quizzes, and browse transit-themed gifts at the pop-up shop.

name: Casino (35mm)
why: 35mm screening of Scorsese's Las Vegas epic starring Robert De Niro and Sharon Stone, introduced by guest programmer Gina Telaroli.

name: Love Me Tonight
why: Rouben Mamoulian's 1932 Rodgers & Hart musical comedy, a complete and total comic delight of the early sound era.

name: In the Cut (35mm)
why: 35mm of Jane Campion's erotic thriller starring Meg Ryan and Mark Ruffalo, initially baffling but now widely admired.

name: The Umbrellas of Cherbourg
why: Jacques Demy's 1964 French New Wave operetta with Catherine Deneuve and Michel Legrand's unforgettable score.

name: Frances Ha
why: Noah Baumbach's generational film starring and co-written by Greta Gerwig, part of the New York Stories series.

name: Wet Hot American Summer (25th Anniversary Labor Day Screening)
why: David Wain's 2001 summer camp comedy starring Paul Rudd, Janeane Garofalo, Molly Shannon, and more, screening on Labor Day for its 25th anniversary.

name: Junk Dump Film Festival
why: Junk Dump Magazine's 6th annual short film festival over two days (Sept 12–13): narrative/documentary shorts on day one, experimental/animation on day two, each followed by filmmaker Q&As.

name: Your Name. (10th Anniversary Screening)
why: 10th anniversary screening of Makoto Shinkai's beloved anime film.

name: Open House New York Weekend 2026
why: Annual three-day festival (Oct 16–18) unlocking 300+ architectural, cultural, and infrastructure sites across the five boroughs for free public access, including this year's newly revealed sites: 77 Water Street office-to-residential conversion, the DSNY BK3 sanitation garage, and the Amant contemporary art center.

name: New York: The Future of Cities
why: Panel featuring filmmaker Ric Burns exploring NYC's evolution from 9/11 through COVID, immigration, and climate change, plus an advance screening of highlights from Burns' new two-part PBS documentary.

name: A Nation in Conversation: David Blight and Khalil Gibran Muhammad
why: Historians David Blight and Khalil Gibran Muhammad explore how narratives of America's past shape our understanding of democracy, citizenship, and identity.

name: Gallery Tour: Revolutionary Women
why: Docent-led tour of the Revolutionary Women exhibition.

name: Gallery Tour: The Weitzman Shoe Museum
why: Docent-led tour of the Weitzman Shoe Museum collection.

name: Gallery Tour: Betye Saar's Black Dolls
why: Docent-led tour of Betye Saar's Black Dolls exhibition.

name: Breakfast University: The Mind of Abraham Lincoln
why: Semester kickoff lecture from Professor Louis Masur (Rutgers) on Lincoln's psychology and decision-making, part of the popular morning Breakfast University series.

name: Another Wonderland: Abram Champanier's Alice Mural
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: 16 newly restored New Deal-era mural panels by Abram Champanier reimagining Lewis Carroll's Alice characters exploring 1930s New York City, originally created for a children's hospital ward between 1938–40.

name: Art as Care: Hospital Murals in Pediatric Healthcare
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Panel bringing together artists, advocates, and hospital leaders to examine what intentional, ambitious art does in spaces where NYC's youngest patients receive care.

name: Ancestral Ecologies
why: Four multisensory outdoor installations by Olalekan Jeyifous and AD--WO (2026 Heidi Nitze Art x Environment Fellows) exploring ancient Latinx and Afrodiasporic beliefs around the intelligence of the natural world; through October 25.

name: Seasonal Highlights Tour
why: Free guided walks of BBG's early-fall foliage, fruits, and flowers led by trained Garden Guides; Tuesdays through Sundays starting September 8.

name: Garden Design 101
why: Workshop on taking a garden design from concept to successful execution.

name: Gardens for Peace
why: A day of free public activities and live music around BBG's Japanese Hill-and-Pond Garden.

name: Designing with Dahlias
why: Hands-on floral design workshop using locally sourced dahlias and seasonal flowers to create a playful, free-flowing arrangement to take home.

name: Shinnecock Oral History Plant Tour
why: Guided plant tour sharing Shinnecock oral history and Indigenous ecological knowledge; also offered October 10.

name: Climate Week Talk: Brooklyn's Greening Heroes
why: Climate Week NYC talk spotlighting Brooklyn residents working on urban greening and environmental resilience.

name: Beginning Birding (5-Week Series)
why: Five-Saturday series learning to find and identify birds at the height of fall migration through BBG's grounds.

name: Amazing Maize Maze at Queens County Farm Museum
why: NYC's only corn maze: a three-acre labyrinth where you follow clues and solve puzzles through the stalks, then look back from Victory Bridge. Weekends through November 1.

name: The Pass at La MaMa
why: American premiere of a sharp, darkly funny Off-Broadway play following two rising British football stars grappling with masculinity, desire, and the machinery of fame; directed by Max Hunter, closing September 18.

name: Fall for Dance Festival
why: Annual dance festival featuring 11 premieres and seven international companies including the Royal Ballet and Gauthier Dance, plus Robbie Fairchild and A.I.M by Kyle Abraham; all tickets $30, Sept 22–Oct 3.

name: ¡Wepa! Summer Salsa Social
why: Afternoon salsa social at the Hispanic Society Museum & Library.

name: Mapping the Revolution: How Maps Shaped the Fight for America
why: NYPL Curator of Maps Ian Fowler explores the role of cartography in the Revolutionary War, presented in connection with the Declaring America: 1776 and Beyond exhibition.

name: Keyholder Exhibition Opening Reception
venue: LESP Gallery, Lower East Side Printshop
why: Opening reception for work by eight Keyholder Residency artists — Mira Dayal, Natasha K. De Armas, Amelia Akiko Frank, Katya Grokhovsky, Leekyung Kang, Melissa Ling, Maha Mohan, and Wenfei Quan — featuring printmaking created during the 2025–26 residency cycle. Exhibition runs through November 13.

name: The Armory Show 2026
why: Major international contemporary art fair at the Javits Center, September 24–27, featuring hundreds of galleries; includes a not-for-profit section with organizations like Lower East Side Printshop.

name: NY Art Book Fair 2026 Opening Night
why: Opening night of the 20th annual NY Art Book Fair, celebrating Printed Matter's 50th anniversary with 300 exhibitors from 41 countries; includes a limited ticket edition by Sara Yukiko and music from Shyboi and A.B.E.L.A. Opening night ticket grants re-entry all weekend.

name: NY Art Book Fair 2026
why: Four-day annual art book fair featuring 300 exhibitors from 41 countries: independent publishers, antiquarian booksellers, galleries, and zine makers — the most geographically diverse lineup in NYABF history. Sept 24–27.

name: Inside the Public Design Commission Archive: NYC's Design Review Agency
why: Behind-the-scenes access to the archive of the agency that reviews and approves public art, design, and architecture on NYC-owned property.

name: Rare Look Inside M&S Schmalberg: NYC's Last Custom Fabric Flower Factory
why: Access inside the last remaining custom fabric flower factory in New York City, a supplier to high fashion houses.

name: After-Hours Pastel Painting Workshop @ AKC Museum of the Dog
why: Evening pastel painting workshop inside the AKC Museum of the Dog's collection.

name: Rosé & Chocolate Tasting @ Roni-Sue's Secret Backyard
why: Rosé and artisan chocolate pairing tasting in the secret backyard of Roni-Sue's Chocolates on the Lower East Side.

name: Private Lawn Bowling Workshop @ Central Park's NY Lawn Bowling Club
venue: New York Lawn Bowling Club, Central Park
why: Private lawn bowling lesson inside Central Park's historic New York Lawn Bowling Club.

name: Exclusive After-Hours Tour @ The United Nations Headquarters
why: Exclusive after-hours guided tour inside the United Nations Headquarters.

name: Look Up! The Hidden History of NYC's Wooden Water Towers
why: Walking tour exploring the hidden history of NYC's iconic rooftop water towers — how they work, who makes them, and what they reveal about the city.

name: Secret Parlor Jazz: Home-Cooked Tunes & BBQ Dinner
why: Intimate jazz concert in a private Upper East Side home with a catered BBQ dinner — a salon-style secret parlor experience.

name: Exclusive Tour Inside the Woolworth Building: NYC's Cathedral of Commerce
why: Guided tour inside the historic Woolworth Building, one of NYC's most architecturally significant skyscrapers and once the world's tallest building.

name: Behind the Scenes @ Fulton Fish Market: World's 2nd Largest Fish Market
venue: Hunts Point Fulton Fish Market, Bronx
why: Early-morning behind-the-scenes tour of Hunts Point Fulton Fish Market — the world's second largest fish market — when the trading action is at its peak.

name: Inside The Players: Rare Look Inside Edwin Booth's Untouched Bedroom
why: Rare access inside The Players, the historic Gramercy Park club founded by actor Edwin Booth in 1888, including his preserved bedroom kept exactly as he left it.

name: Secret Eats of Arthur Avenue: The Bronx's Little Italy
why: Guided food crawl through Arthur Avenue, the Bronx's authentic Little Italy neighborhood, sampling specialties from old-school Italian delis, bakeries, and butchers.

name: Exclusive Trip Inside the Loew's Valencia: NYC's First Wonder Theatre
why: Exclusive behind-the-scenes access to the Loew's Valencia, one of NYC's legendary atmospheric movie palaces — a Spanish Renaissance-style wonder built in 1929.

name: Speakeasies & Swing Street: Exploring NYC's Prohibition Nightlife History
why: Walking tour tracing NYC's Prohibition-era speakeasies and the jazz clubs of Swing Street.

name: Behind-the-Scenes @ Lincoln Center: Extended Tour Inside Iconic Halls
why: Extended backstage tour of Lincoln Center's performance halls, including areas not accessible to the public.

name: Exclusive Truffle 101 & Hands-On Tasting @ Urbani Truffle Lab NYC
why: Truffle education class and hands-on tasting at Urbani, the world's foremost truffle purveyor.

name: Secrets of the East River: NYC's Hidden Infrastructure by Ferry
why: Ferry tour revealing the hidden infrastructure along the East River — power plants, bridges, and waterfront history rarely seen from ground level.

name: Behind-the-Scenes @ Temple Emanu-El: One of the World's Largest Synagogues
why: Behind-the-scenes tour inside Temple Emanu-El, one of the world's largest synagogues and a landmark of Fifth Avenue.

name: Walking Brooklyn's Gowanus Canal: From Toxic Past to Luxury Living
why: Walking tour along the Gowanus Canal tracing its transformation from one of NYC's most polluted waterways to a Superfund site surrounded by luxury development.

name: Beginner Embroidery Workshop
why: Hands-on embroidery workshop for beginners; all materials included.

name: Floral Embroidery Workshop
why: Intermediate embroidery class focusing on floral motifs and texture techniques; all materials included.

name: Beaded Embroidery Workshop
why: Embroidery workshop incorporating bead techniques for added dimension; all materials included.

name: New Openings Against Old Surfaces: On Gordon Matta-Clark's Walls Paper
why: The first exhibition focused on Gordon Matta-Clark's 1973 publication Walls Paper — photographs abstracting interior walls of half-demolished South Bronx and LES tenements — with archival prints, test sheets, and documentary photos from its original installation at 112 Greene Street. On view Sept 9–Nov 29.

name: Gordon Matta-Clark: Physical Poetics — Conversation with Jessamyn Fiore & Frances Richard
why: Public conversation between Jessamyn Fiore (Director of the Estate of Gordon Matta-Clark) and scholar Frances Richard on Matta-Clark's relationship to books, language, and the printed page.

name: New Openings Against Old Surfaces — Opening Reception
why: Opening reception for the Gordon Matta-Clark Walls Paper exhibition with remarks from Estate Director Jessamyn Fiore.

name: Beginner Patchwork Workshop
why: Beginner patchwork sewing workshop; all materials included.

name: Macramé Plant Hanger Workshop
why: Macramé workshop making a knotted plant hanger; all materials included.

name: Sew a Jumpsuit (4-Part Workshop)
why: Four-session garment sewing course to construct a jumpsuit from scratch; all materials included.

name: Intro to Garment Sewing: Free Range Slacks (3-Part Weeknight Course)
why: Three-part weeknight garment sewing course making the Free Range Slacks pattern; all materials included. Starts Sept 14.

name: Knitting 104: Sock Knitting
why: Advanced knitting workshop focused on sock construction using double-pointed needles; all materials included.

name: 5-Week Sewing Course: Ilford Jacket
why: Five-week Thursday evening sewing course constructing the Ilford Jacket pattern; all materials included. Starts Sept 17.

name: Knitting 102: Billie Bandana
why: Knitting workshop making the Billie Bandana; suitable for those who know knit and purl stitches. All materials included.

name: MAS Grand Central Terminal Tour
why: Small-group in-person tour of Grand Central Terminal led by MAS Docents, offered at a reduced price throughout September and October. Space is limited.

name: East from Gramercy Park Walking Tour
why: New MAS walking tour with historian Matt Postal exploring the architectural and social history east of Gramercy Park.

name: Histories of Social Housing in NYC Walking Tour
why: MAS walking tour with Katelin Penner examining the history of public and social housing on the Lower East Side.

name: Adaptive Reuse on the Hudson River Tour
why: MAS tour with Ginny Poleman examining adaptive reuse projects along the Hudson River waterfront.

name: Frida & Diego: Last Dream
why: MoMA exhibition on Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera, closing Sept 12.

name: Giacometti at the Temple of Dendur
why: Giacometti sculpture exhibition in the Met's Temple of Dendur gallery, closing Sept 8.

name: Everything * AI Conference
why: Full-day AI conference at Pioneer Works featuring speakers including Paul Ford (Aboard), Tido Carriero (VP Engineering, Cursor), Andrew Qu (Chief of Software, Vercel), and Magnus Hillestad (CEO, Sanity).

name: Forbes Power Women's Summit
why: Annual Forbes summit featuring Leena Nair (CEO, Chanel), Cindy Crawford, and Jennifer Garner.

name: Fast Company Innovation Festival
why: Multi-day Fast Company summit featuring Cristiano Amon (CEO, Qualcomm), Paul Dillinger (Head of Design Innovation, Levi Strauss), Mike Intrator (CEO, CoreWeave), and Rachel Kornafel (Chief Brand Officer, Union Square Hospitality Group).

name: Women in AI Pitch Competition
why: Free pitch competition showcase featuring women-founded AI startups, with judges including Dennis Thankachan (CEO, Lightyear) and Joy Marcus (The 98).

name: NY Tech Meetup: Climate Tech Edition
why: Free NY Tech Meetup focused on climate tech startups and solutions, at Civic Hall.

name: The New Yorker Festival
why: Annual New Yorker Festival with talks, screenings, and performances across Manhattan, Oct 23–25.

name: An American Daughter
why: First New York revival of Wendy Wasserstein's acclaimed 1997 play, in a bold new staging that includes a previously unpublished second act. Starring Montego Glover, Robert Sean Leonard, and Jean Lichty. Running through Sept 20.
